newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T plays down lawsuit settlement talk.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T plays down lawsuit settlement talk.

text.p: British tobacco company B.A.T Industries Plc on Wednesday played down market speculation that the tobacco industry was drawing up plans to settle its ligitation woes.
"As to settlement, the market is getting ahead of itself," B.A.T spokesman Michael Prideaux told Reuters.
"No one has actually proposed anything to the tobacco industry."

Tobacco stocks rallied in the U.S. on Tuesday following last week's West Virginia court ruling against parts of the state's Medicaid lawsuit and amid reports the industry is taking steps to settle its litigation woes.

According to industry sources and analysts, major tobacco companies have hired two law firms and a public relations firm to consider possible parameters for a broad settlement of the potential landslide of tobacco-related lawsuits hanging over the industry.
Prideaux said it was no secret that the tobacco industry had hired law firms but doubted any comprehensive settlement was likely any time soon.
"While nothing is impossible. It would take a very long time to bring this off, if indeed it is possible at all," he said.
"The industry would only be interested in something that provided immunity from all current and future lawsuits at a price that was in its shareholders' interest."
Tobacco stocks have been selling at a discount because investors fear the enormous litigation weighing on the companies' fiscal health.
At present 21 U.S. states have filed lawsuits against the manufacturers and promoters of cigarettes and chewing tobacco seeking to recoup money spent on health care costs attributable to tobacco.
